quote: it's saving me only a $100 a month,
stewart_read: Customer hands the rep the exact bill-pain number and the rep never reflects it back as leverage against the utility bill.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read is more supported since the rep pivots immediately to incentive talk rather than any deliberate later setup — the number is never revisited at all.
coaching_implication: Rep should have flipped: 'so right now you're stuck paying that $100 forever — solar just replaces that expense' instead of moving straight to tax credit talk.

quote: I'm actually glad that you brought that up just because yeah. The only incentive actually that was removed was the federal tax credit
stewart_read: Customer's cost objection gets a factual incentive rebuttal, not the emotional flip the schema prescribes (bill pain vs cost pain).
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read is weak here — the rep is improvising with incomplete incentive knowledge rather than executing a deliberate inversion strategy.
coaching_implication: Coach the flip pattern: reframe the $20k cost against the customer's own $100/month recurring loss, not just against tax-credit facts.

quote: it's kinda funny. So I'm just like a scheduler.
stewart_read: Rep names the scope boundary correctly here, but only after already speculating on offset percentages and payback specifics earlier in the call.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be read as strategic humility-building rapport, but the inconsistency (guessing earlier, disclaiming later) undercuts that reading.
coaching_implication: Apply the escape hatch earlier and consistently — anything about offset %, cost, or payback duration should route to the specialist from the first ask.

quote: Yeah. Is that kinda what you're looking for is just getting a 100% offset?
stewart_read: Rep continues speculating about offset percentages and comparing customer to 'some houses' after already disclaiming expertise, re-entering closer territory.
alternative_hypothesis: n/a — clear reactive scope creep, not a deliberate strategy.
coaching_implication: Once the scheduler disclaimer is used, hold it — don't re-engage on system sizing specifics; bridge straight to the specialist.

quote: Do you know, like, about how much of my energy needs the solar would be able to cover?
stewart_read: Customer proactively asking about offset coverage near the end signals genuine buying interest has built across the call.
coaching_implication: This is the moment to bridge cleanly to the specialist and tie the appointment to answering exactly this — instead the rep answers with speculation.

quote: Yes. And, actually so I'm closing on this house this coming Monday, so it's not mine yet.
stewart_read: Customer is not yet the legal owner and closes Monday — a material timing fact for the co-owner/homeowner qualifier that the rep captured but didn't flag as a risk to the appointment.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be read as fine since ownership completes before the appointment, but the rep never confirms this timing is resolved before Tuesday's call.
coaching_implication: Rep should explicitly confirm ownership will be finalized before the specialist call, given DQ rule around not_homeowner.

quote: Yeah. You get lots of sun on that garage. I actually want to say that that might be a better place for the panels than even your home roof.
stewart_read: Rep speculates on optimal panel placement based on Google Maps, a technical/design judgment that belongs to the specialist.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be seen as rapport-building neighbor-like engagement, but it crosses into design opinion territory.
coaching_implication: Acknowledge the garage as additional usable space and let the specialist determine placement, rather than rendering a design verdict.
